text: Names the target stack precisely enough to write real build, lint and test commands for it: language, framework, package manager, test runner.
States the exact commands that belong in the project's compass/config.yaml checks: list, the same commands the CI-parity gate runs before any pull request can open.
Lists every repo to create, each with a key, a name and an area (backend, mobile, frontend), as a closed list the next row registers.
Lists every top-level file and directory execute-scaffold will create: a plan to carry out, not only a description of the architecture.
Names what each repo exposes or consumes across repos (for example the API surface a client repo depends on), because each execute run sees only its own repo.

Writes compass/config.yaml with the checks: list the accepted scaffold-record specified for this repo, and a .github/workflows file that runs those same checks on pull_request — CI is what verifies this pull request, since there is no local checkout to verify it in.
Every file created matches what the accepted scaffold-record said it would create: no scope drift between the accepted plan and what lands in the pull request.

Every repo the accepted scaffold plan lists is created on GitHub and registered on the engagement with its key, name, area and GitHub URL — a local checkout follows later, once build or fix needs one; the scaffold itself writes through the GitHub API.
Every check run on the pull request passed.
